chunks: Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the reason for sawm (fasting), so he said:

"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only prescribed sawm (fasting) so that through it the rich and the poor may become equal. That is because the rich would not experience the touch of hunger and so have mercy on the poor, since the rich, whenever they desire something, are able to obtain it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wanted to make equality among His creation and to let the rich taste the touch of hunger and pain, so that he may become tender toward the weak and thus have mercy on the hungry."

key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: sawm (fasting) as an obligatory act of worship
key_terms.الْغَنِيُّ: the wealthy person who has access to what he desires
key_terms.مَسَّ الْجُوعِ: the experience or touch of hunger

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah make fasting obligatory according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that sawm (fasting) was made obligatory so that the rich may directly experience hunger and thereby develop mercy toward the poor and the weak. It presents fasting not only as an act of worship but also as a means of cultivating compassion and social equality among people.
